localities.name: New York City (all five boroughs)
localities.covers: Work performed anywhere in the five boroughs. This is a higher rate set by New York State for the city specifically, not a city ordinance — so it is enforced by the state labour department.

facts.summary: The minimum wage in New York City is $17.00 an hour from 1 January 2026 — higher than the rest of New York State. From 2027 it rises with inflation, tracked against the Northeast CPI-W.
facts.citation: New York Labor Law § 652 (state minimum wage)
facts.sourceAgency: New York State Dept of Labor
facts.notes: Set by state law for the NYC region rather than by a city ordinance. facts.summary: Tipped food-service workers in New York City must be paid at least $11.35 an hour in cash wages, with a tip credit of up to $5.65. Your tips have to bring you to $17.00 an hour — if they do not, your employer owes the difference.
facts.citation: New York hospitality industry wage order (12 NYCRR pt. 146)
facts.sourceAgency: New York State Dept of Labor

facts.summary: Other tipped service employees in New York City must be paid at least $14.15 an hour in cash wages, with a tip credit of up to $2.85, and tips must bring you to $17.00 an hour in total.
facts.citation: New York hospitality industry wage order (12 NYCRR pt. 146)
